summary: Town Hill, Sandisfield MA: 30-ft wooden tower first operated 1915 and staffed until 1917; 2003 search found only a rusted phone line; FFLOS-registered 2008.

facts.status_note: The register says the tower no longer stands; a 2003 search of the site found only an old rusted phone line

events.note: First operated in 1915 per FFLOS; a telephone line of 1.5 miles was run to the site when the tower was constructed (no year given for that work)
Fall 2003: FFLA members searched for remains for several hours; only an old rusted phone line was found

evidence.supports: 30-foot wooden tower that no longer stands
evidence.quote: This 30' wooden tower no longer stands.
This tower was first operated in 1915 and was staffed until 1917.

evidence.supports: 1.5 miles of phone line run to the site when the tower was constructed
evidence.quote: When the tower was constructed, 1.5 miles of phone line were run to the site.

evidence.quote: In the fall of 2003, a group of FFLA members

evidence.supports: 2003 search found only the old rusted phone line
evidence.quote: After scouting for several hours, the only remains that were found of this tower was the old rusted phone line.

notes_for_editor: Single register entry, but a detailed one with a 2003 site check. Town pages (sandisfieldma.gov town history and the 1762-2012 history PDF) returned HTTP 403, so local history is unchecked. The Wikipedia article on Sandisfield has no fire tower mention. No source names staff, fires or access. 30 ft converted to 9.1 m. Story says 'first operated' because no build date is given, and the phone-line work is dated only to the tower's construction.
